intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently for an authentic culinary adventure.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An on the 14th of each lunar month when the town turns off electric lights and glows with hundreds of colorful silk lanterns. Rent a bicycle to roam the historic streets, visit tailor shops, and sample White Rose dumplings and Cao Lau noodles from street stalls along the Thu Bon River.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic coastal mountain roads. The route offers breathtaking views of the South China Sea, jungle-covered peaks, and old French military bunkers, connecting Da Nang and Hue in a thrilling half-day adventure.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Sampan Boat Tour
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, hopping on a traditional wooden sampan boat through narrow canals lined with coconut palms. Visit floating markets, local workshops producing rice paper and coconut candy, and sample tropical fruits while experiencing the rural waterway culture of southern Vietnam.

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Night Scene
experiences.description: Dive into the heart of Ho Chi Minh City's backpacker district on Bui Vien Street, a vibrant pedestrian strip packed with budget guesthouses, open-air bars, and street food stalls. Sip on fresh sugarcane juice, try Banh Trang Tron (rice paper salad), and soak up the electric atmosphere of neon lights, live music, and fellow travelers from around the world.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.date: Day 1 - April 15 (Arrival Day)
day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the 86 airport bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check into Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk through the winding streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai, Hang Bac, and Dinh Liet streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Hoan Kiem Lake for the iconic Turtle Tower view at dusk. Walk across The Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (entry ~30,000 VND). Head to Ta Hien Street — known as 'Beer Street' — for a cheap bia hoi (fresh draught beer, ~10,000 VND per glass) and soak up the backpacker atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a banh mi from a street cart near the Old Quarter upon arrival (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun cha at a local street stall on Hang Manh or Ly Quoc Su Street (~50,000–70,000 VND). Try the grilled pork with rice noodles and fresh herbs.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash at the airport or use an ATM in the Old Quarter. Avoid taxis at the airport — use the 86 bus or pre-book a Grab ride (~250,000 VND) for safety. Keep your bags close in the busy Old Quarter streets.

day_by_day.date: Day 2 - April 16 (Hanoi Deep Dive)
day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a bowl of pho at a local street kitchen. Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the morning exercise scene — locals practice tai chi, badminton, and aerobics around the lake from 6:00–8:00 AM. Visit Ngoc Son Temple if you missed it last night. Walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral (free entry) for its French colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND) — one of Southeast Asia's best cultural museums showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Take a local bus (xe buyt) there for ~9,000 VND. Alternatively, visit the Temple of Literature (~30,000 VND), Vietnam's first university, a stunning example of traditional Vietnamese architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the famous Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday–Sunday). Browse handicrafts, clothing, and souvenirs. Settle in at a low plastic-stool street food spot for dinner. End the night with a Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da) at a sidewalk café.

meals.breakfast: Pho bo (beef noodle soup) at a street stall on Bat Dan Street — famous for pho (~50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) near the museum area (~50,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh xeo (sizzling Vietnamese crepe) and fresh spring rolls at a street stall on Ma May Street (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Night Market runs Friday to Sunday — if Day 2 falls on a weekday, substitute with a walk through Dong Xuan Market (Hanoi's largest indoor market). Bargain respectfully at markets — start at 50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 - April 17 (Hanoi Hidden Gems)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex early (opens 7:30 AM, closed Mon/Fri). See the One Pillar Pagoda (free) and Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House (~40,000 VND). The Ba Dinh area is walkable and historically rich. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hoa Lo Prison Museum (~30,000 VND), also known as the 'Hanoi Hilton,' for a sobering look at Vietnamese and American war history. Afterward, wander through the French Quarter to admire colonial-era architecture along Trang Tien and Ngo Quyen streets.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Theatre (~100,000 VND) — a uniquely Vietnamese art form dating back to the 11th century. Afterward, explore the vibrant street food scene on Dinh Liet Street for late-night snacks.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor near the hotel (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun rieu (crab and tomato noodle soup) at a local quan (eatery) near Hoa Lo (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com binh dan (Vietnamese set meal with rice, veggies, and protein) at a local canteen (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Mausoleum is closed Monday and Friday, and for about 2 months annually (Sept–Nov) for maintenance. Check ahead. Dress code is strictly enforced. Book the Water Puppet Show in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18 (Day Trip: Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or book a budget day tour to Ninh Binh (~2 hours from Hanoi, bus ~80,000–120,000 VND one way from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000/day) to explore the Tam Coc area. Take a 2-hour rowing boat trip through the stunning limestone karst caves of Tam Coc (~150,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free entry) nestled into the cliffs. Continue to Mua Cave (~100,000 VND) and climb 500 steps for a panoramic view over the rice paddies and karst landscape — one of Vietnam's most iconic vistas. This is often called 'Halong Bay on land.'
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus. Arrive back in the Old Quarter by 7:00–8:00 PM. Reward yourself with a hearty dinner and a cold bia hoi.

meals.breakfast: Grab a banh mi or sticky rice from a street stall before catching the bus (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh goat meat or eel rice (dac san Ninh Binh) at a local restaurant in Tam Coc (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pho or bun cha back in Hanoi's Old Quarter (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Start as early as 6:30–7:00 AM to make the most of the day. Alternatively, book a budget group day tour from the Old Quarter (~300,000–400,000 VND all-in) which includes transport and a guide. Bring sunscreen and water — the Mua Cave climb is strenuous.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 - April 19 (Travel to Hoi An via Da Nang)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hanoi hotel. Take a Grab to Hanoi Train Station or catch a bus to Noi Bai for a budget flight to Da Nang (book in advance with VietJet or Bamboo Airways, ~500,000–900,000 VND). Alternatively, take the overnight train to Da Nang (~300,000–500,000 VND for a hard sleeper) if departing the previous evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Da Nang. Take a local bus or cheap Grab to Hoi An (~30 km, ~150,000–200,000 VND by Grab or ~50,000 VND by local bus). Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in Hoi An's An Hoi area (~150,000–250,000 VND/night). Drop your bags and head to the Ancient Town.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hoi An Ancient Town at dusk — the lantern-lit streets are magical. Walk along the Thu Bon River, cross the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, and browse the silk lantern shops. Evening is the best time as the town glows with hundreds of colorful lanterns.

meals.breakfast: Quick banh mi or xoi near the Hanoi hotel before checkout (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport or train station food, or pack snacks for the journey
meals.dinner: Cao lau (Hoi An's signature noodle dish) at a street stall in the Ancient Town (~50,000–70,000 VND) — this dish is unique to Hoi An

day_by_day.notes: Book flights or train tickets well in advance for the best budget prices. The Hoi An Ancient Town entry ticket (~120,000 VND) gives access to 5 heritage sites — buy it if you plan to visit museums and pagodas. Many outer areas are free to walk through.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 - April 20 (Hoi An Culture & Craft)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hoi An Ancient Town in the morning before crowds arrive. Explore the Japanese Covered Bridge (ticket required), Phung Hung Old House, and the Assembly Halls. Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000/day) — Hoi An is perfectly flat and best explored on two wheels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle 4 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a few hours of relaxation. Swim, read, or simply enjoy the coastline. Cycle back through the rice paddies and vegetable villages. Visit Tra Que Vegetable Village (~30,000 VND entry) to see organic farming and join a simple cooking demo if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget cooking class (~300,000–500,000 VND) — Hoi An is famous for its food culture and many affordable classes include a market visit. Alternatively, take an evening lantern boat ride on the Thu Bon River (~50,000–100,000 VND) and release a paper lantern for good luck.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi Phuong (~35,000 VND) — made famous by Anthony Bourdain, located on Phan Chau Trinh Street. Arrive early as queues form quickly.
meals.lunch: White rose dumplings (banh bao vac) and fried wontons at a local stall (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com ga (Hoi An chicken rice) at a local restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND) or street food from the night market on Nguyen Hoang Street

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is extremely walkable and bikeable. Avoid tuk-tuks and motorbike taxis unless necessary — cycling is cheaper and more enjoyable. The Ancient Town gets very crowded midday; explore early morning or evening for the best experience.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21 (Day Trip: My Son Sanctuary & Marble Mountains)
day_by_day.morning: Take a budget group tour or rent a motorbike to My Son Sanctuary (~45 km from Hoi An, ~150,000 VND entry). These ancient Cham temple ruins date back to the 4th–14th centuries and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the jungle-surrounded ruins in the cooler morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return toward Da Nang and stop at the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) — five limestone and marble hills with caves, pagodas, and tunnels (~40,000 VND entry). Climb to the top for panoramic views of Da Nang city and the ocean. Browse the marble carving workshops at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An by late afternoon. Relax and explore the riverside promenade. Visit the colorful Hoi An Night Market for souvenirs, street food, and atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Banh cuon (steamed rice rolls) or mi quang (turmeric noodles) at a local breakfast spot (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Pack a banh mi or eat at a local restaurant near My Son (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Mi quang (Quang-style noodles with shrimp, pork, and peanuts) at a street stall in Hoi An (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited early morning — it gets very hot and crowded by midday. A budget group tour from Hoi An typically costs ~150,000–250,000 VND including transport. Renting a motorbike (~120,000–150,000/day) gives more flexibility if you're a confident rider.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 - April 22 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hoi An guesthouse. Take a Grab or local bus to Da Nang Airport. Catch a budget flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) — book with VietJet or Bamboo Airways (~400,000–800,000 VND if booked in advance). Flight is approximately 1 hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Take the 109 airport bus (~20,000 VND) or a Grab (~120,000–150,000 VND) to the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district — budget accommodation hub (~150,000–300,000 VND/night). Check in, drop bags, and head out to explore District 1.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Ben Thanh Market (closing around 6 PM for the indoor section, but the outdoor night market continues until late). Browse street food stalls, try local snacks, and get a feel for the city's incredible energy. Explore the surrounding streets of District 1.

meals.breakfast: Quick banh mi or coffee near the Hoi An guesthouse before checkout
meals.lunch: Airport food or snacks during transit
meals.dinner: Hu tieu (southern Vietnamese noodle soup) or com tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at a street stall near Pham Ngu Lao (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City traffic is intense — crossing the street requires confidence (walk slowly and steadily, don't stop). Pham Ngu Lao is the best budget base with hostels, travel agencies, and cheap eateries. Watch your belongings carefully in crowded areas.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23 (Ho Chi Minh City History & Culture)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a powerful and moving museum documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Allow 2 hours. Walk to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) to explore the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, frozen in time since 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica (free, may be under renovation — admire from outside) and the Central Post Office (free entry) — a stunning French colonial building designed by Gustave Eiffel. Walk through the upscale Dong Khoi Street area. Take a local bus or walk to Chinatown (Cho Lon) to explore Binh Tay Market and the ornate Thien Hau Temple (free).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bui Vien Walking Street — the famous backpacker strip — for cheap beer (~20,000–30,000 VND), street food, and lively nightlife. Try a Vietnamese iced coffee at a sidewalk café. Experience the chaotic, electric energy of Saigon at night.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi op la (egg banh mi) from a street cart (~25,000–35,000 VND) with Vietnamese drip coffee (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com tam (broken rice) with grilled pork, pickled veggies, and fried egg at a local com tam shop (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Goi cuon (fresh spring rolls) and banh xeo (sizzling crepe) at a street food stall on Dinh Cong Trang Street (~60,000–90,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — take your time and be respectful. Chinatown is best reached by local bus (routes 1 or 14) for ~6,000–8,000 VND. Grab is reliable and affordable for longer distances within the city.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 - April 24 (Cu Chi Tunnels & Departure Prep)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early budget group tour or local bus to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~70 km from HCMC, entry ~110,000 VND). Explore the remarkable 250 km underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong soldiers during the war. Crawl through the tunnels, see booby traps, and learn about guerrilla warfare. A group tour from Pham Ngu Lao costs ~150,000–250,000 VND including transport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ho Chi Minh City by early afternoon. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market or the local shops on Pham Ngu Lao. Visit a local café for a final Vietnamese iced coffee or egg coffee (ca phe trung). Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final Vietnamese meal in the city. Head to the airport via Grab or the 109 bus depending on your flight time. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Vietnam's culture, history, and street food scene.

meals.breakfast: Pho or bun bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) at a local spot before departing for Cu Chi (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Simple local meal near Cu Chi Tunnels or pack snacks (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) at a budget restaurant in District 1 — perfect for a celebratory final meal (~100,000–150,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels Ben Duoc site is less touristy than Ben Dinh — consider visiting Ben Duoc for a more authentic experience. Book your airport transfer in advance if departing late at night. Keep some VND for airport snacks and last-minute expenses. Total estimated daily budget: ~400,000–700,000 VND (~$16–$28 USD) excluding accommodation and transport between cities.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in the Old Quarter (approximately 45 minutes by taxi or Grab, ~200,000–300,000 VND). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a hotel map of the Old Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely self-guided walking tour of the 36 Ancient Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the bustling Dong Xuan Market. Pick up snacks from street vendors and soak in the chaotic, colorful energy of Hanoi's oldest neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the evening atmosphere — watch locals exercise, chat, and relax around the lake. Cross the iconic red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (if still open). Stroll Ta Hien Street (Beer Street) for your first taste of Hanoi's vibrant nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a light snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Street food near the hotel — try Banh Mi from a local cart (15,000–25,000 VND) or a bowl of Pho Bo from a sidewalk stall.
meals.dinner: Bun Cha Huong Lien (the famous 'Obama Bun Cha' restaurant) on Le Van Huu Street — grilled pork patties with rice noodles and fresh herbs (~80,000–120,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: Use Grab app for affordable and reliable transport from the airport. Exchange some VND at the airport or use ATMs in the Old Quarter. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Old Quarter streets are uneven and lively.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a classic Hanoi breakfast at a local pho shop near the hotel. Then visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (open mornings only, closed Mondays and Fridays). See the One Pillar Pagoda and the Presidential Palace gardens. Arrive early (before 10:00) to avoid long queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (Nguyen Van Huyen Road) — one of Southeast Asia's best cultural museums, showcasing 54 ethnic groups with outdoor exhibits and traditional houses (~40,000 VND entry). Take a Grab there (~50,000 VND each way). Return to the Old Quarter and explore the Hanoi Old Quarter Heritage House on Ma May Street.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the famous Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre on Dinh Tien Hoang Street near Hoan Kiem Lake. Shows run approximately 50 minutes and tickets cost ~100,000 VND. Book in advance or arrive 30 minutes early. Afterward, explore the night food stalls around the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo or Pho Ga at a local street-side pho shop near the hotel (~40,000–60,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Bun Rieu (crab noodle soup) from a street stall in the Old Quarter, or grab Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a local eatery (~40,000–70,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — Hanoi's iconic turmeric-marinated fish dish cooked tableside (~180,000–250,000 VND per person). A must-try Hanoi classic.

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed Monday and Friday mornings and throughout September and October for maintenance — check the schedule. Dress modestly for the mausoleum (no shorts or sleeveless tops). Book water puppet show tickets online or at the box office.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh — depart early by bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station (~70,000–90,000 VND, 2 hours). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) to explore the Trang An Landscape Complex. Take a boat tour through the stunning limestone karst caves and rice paddies of Trang An (~200,000 VND per person, ~2.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital — the 10th-century royal citadel with two beautifully preserved temples dedicated to the Dinh and Le dynasties (~15,000 VND entry). Optionally climb the 500 steps to Mua Cave viewpoint for panoramic views of the Ninh Binh landscape (~100,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus in the late afternoon/early evening. Rest at the hotel, then head out for a relaxed dinner and evening walk around Hoan Kiem Lake.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street cart near the hotel before departure (~20,000–35,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or fresh spring rolls at a local Ninh Binh restaurant near Trang An (~60,000–100,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Bun Oc (snail noodle soup) at a local Old Quarter eatery — a Hanoi specialty (~50,000–80,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Start this day very early (by 7:00–7:30) to maximize time in Ninh Binh. Alternatively, book a guided day tour from Hanoi (~400,000–600,000 VND including transport) for convenience. Bring sunscreen and water — outdoor activities in April can be warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi for Ha Long Bay — take a mid-range overnight cruise (book in advance, ~2,500,000–3,500,000 VND for a 2D/1N cruise). Board the cruise around noon. Morning: pack up and check out of the Hanoi hotel, store luggage if needed, and take a shuttle bus to Ha Long (~3.5 hours from Hanoi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ha Long Bay and board the cruise. Sail through the iconic emerald waters and towering limestone karsts. Visit Sung Sot (Surprise) Cave — one of the largest and most impressive caves in Ha Long Bay. Enjoy kayaking or bamboo boat rides through hidden lagoons.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Ha Long Bay from the cruise deck. Enjoy a seafood cooking demonstration, squid fishing off the back of the boat, and a communal dinner with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Pho near the Old Quarter before departure (~30,000–50,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Light snacks on the shuttle bus or at the Ha Long pier before boarding.
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood dinner included on the cruise — typically featuring grilled prawns, steamed clams, squid, and Vietnamese-style fish dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable mid-range cruise line such as Indochina Junk, Bhaya Cruises, or Era Cruises. Prices typically include meals, kayaking, and cave visits. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. April weather in Ha Long is generally pleasant with warm temperatures and low chance of rain.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early on the cruise for a sunrise over Ha Long Bay — a truly magical experience. Enjoy Tai Chi on the deck, then a hearty breakfast. Visit a second highlight such as Luon Cave by kayak or a floating fishing village. Check out of your cabin by 09:00–10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ha Long pier by early afternoon. Take the shuttle bus back to Hanoi (arriving ~17:00). Alternatively, take an evening flight from Van Don Airport to Da Nang or Hue to continue south (book domestic flight in advance, ~500,000–900,000 VND with VietJet or Bamboo Airways). Check into a mid-range hostel or guesthouse in Hue.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hue. Take a short walk along the Perfume River embankment. Explore the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker street area for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Included on the cruise — Vietnamese breakfast spread with eggs, bread, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch included on the cruise before disembarkation, or a quick bite at the Ha Long pier.
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (Hue-style spicy beef noodle soup) at a local Hue restaurant — the city's most iconic dish (~50,000–80,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Confirm shuttle bus departure times with your cruise operator. If flying to Hue, Van Don Airport is ~60 km from Ha Long pier — factor in transfer time. Alternatively, travel by sleeper train from Hanoi to Hue overnight (~200,000–350,000 VND) if you prefer a slower pace and want to save on accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Hue. Morning: visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Dai Noi) — the UNESCO-listed former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty (~150,000 VND entry). Explore the Flag Tower, Ngo Mon Gate, Thai Hoa Palace, and the Forbidden Purple City ruins. Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) to get around.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or take a Grab to visit the Royal Tombs along the Perfume River. The Tomb of Minh Mang and Tomb of Tu Duc are the most impressive (~100,000 VND each). Alternatively, take a dragon boat ride along the Perfume River to Thien Mu Pagoda (~150,000 VND) — Hue's iconic seven-tiered pagoda and one of Vietnam's most photographed landmarks.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Dong Ba Market for an authentic local shopping and food experience. Walk along the Truong Tien Bridge lit up at night. Enjoy Hue's famous royal cuisine for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Hue or Com Hen (baby clam rice) — a Hue breakfast specialty (~25,000–40,000 VND) from a street stall.
meals.lunch: Banh Khoai (Hue sizzling crepes) and Nem Lui (lemongrass pork skewers) at a local Hue eatery near the citadel (~60,000–100,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Com Hen (clam rice) or a Hue Royal Set Meal at a riverside restaurant — try Tinh Gia Vien or a similar local spot (~150,000–250,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: April in Hue can be hot — carry water and wear a hat. The Imperial Citadel is large; allow at least 2–3 hours. Combine 2–3 royal tombs in one afternoon if cycling between them. Hue is a very walkable and bikeable city — ideal for backpackers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hue for Hoi An via the Hai Van Pass — one of the most scenic coastal mountain roads in Vietnam. Hire a motorbike taxi (xe om) or join a group tour (~300,000–500,000 VND) for the journey. Stop at the Lang Co Beach lagoon viewpoint and the summit of Hai Van Pass for panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Da Nang — stop briefly at My Khe Beach or the Dragon Bridge. Then continue south to Hoi An Ancient Town (~30 km from Da Nang). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hostel in or near the Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and the colorful merchant houses.
day_by_day.evening: Hoi An comes alive at night with hundreds of colorful lanterns. Join the evening lantern release ceremony on the Thu Bon River (buy a lantern for ~20,000–30,000 VND). Browse the Night Market on Nguyen Hoang Street.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Pho near your Hue guesthouse before departure.
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch at a local restaurant in Da Nang — Banh Xeo (sizzling pancakes) or fresh seafood (~80,000–120,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature noodle dish made with local well water) and White Rose Dumplings at Thanh Restaurant or a local Ancient Town eatery (~80,000–130,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass route by motorbike is the most scenic but requires comfort on two wheels. Alternatively, take a private car or join an Easy Rider tour. The Hoi An Ancient Town entrance ticket (~120,000 VND) gives access to 5 heritage sites — purchase at the ticket booths at the town entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) to cycle through the Hoi An countryside — ride through rice paddies, vegetable farms, and traditional villages to the Tra Que Herb Village (~3 km from town). Join a 2-hour hands-on cooking and farming experience (~200,000–300,000 VND) at a local farm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (5–7 km from the Ancient Town by bicycle) for a relaxing afternoon swim. Rent a sun lounger (~50,000–80,000 VND) at a beachside café. Return to town in the late afternoon and browse the tailor shops and lantern markets of the Ancient Town.
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food walking tour of Hoi An (~300,000–500,000 VND) — sample Banh Mi Phuong (arguably Vietnam's most famous Banh Mi), Mi Quang noodles, and sweet Che desserts. End the evening with a drink at a riverside bar overlooking the illuminated Ancient Town.

meals.breakfast: Fresh baguette and strong Vietnamese iced coffee (Ca Phe Sua Da) at a local café (~30,000–50,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a beachside shack at An Bang Beach — grilled fish, prawns, and cold beer (~100,000–180,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner, or dine independently on Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork, shrimp, and herbs) at a local stall (~40,000–60,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Banh Mi Phuong (115 Hoi An Street) is a legendary stop — go early or expect a queue. April is generally warm and sunny in Hoi An — perfect beach weather. If interested in having clothes tailored, visit shops on Day 7 so they're ready by Day 8 or 9.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning flight or overnight sleeper bus from Hoi An/Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Flights from Da Nang to HCMC take ~1 hour (~500,000–900,000 VND with budget airlines). Alternatively, take a 16–18 hour sleeper bus (~250,000–350,000 VND). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hostel in the Bui Vien (backpacker) or District 1 area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. Visit the Reunification Palace (formerly Independence Palace, ~40,000 VND entry) — a fascinating Cold War-era time capsule. Walk to the nearby Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica and the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel). Stroll along Dong Khoi Street.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's famous backpacker strip — for an energetic evening of street food, cold Saigon beer, and live music. Alternatively, visit the Ben Thanh Night Market for street food and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Pho at a Hoi An street stall before departure, or airport food.
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork chop, egg, and pickled vegetables) at a local District 1 eatery — HCMC's quintessential lunch dish (~50,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (sizzling Vietnamese crepes) and fresh spring rolls at Banh Xeo 46A on Dinh Cong Trang Street — a local institution (~100,000–150,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang–HCMC flight well in advance for the best prices. If taking the sleeper bus, depart from Hoi An on the night of Day 8 and arrive in HCMC on the morning of Day 9 — adjust the itinerary accordingly. Use Grab for all transport within HCMC — metered taxis can overcharge tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (28 Vo Van Tan Street, ~40,000 VND entry) — one of the most powerful and thought-provoking museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War. Allow 2 hours. Then explore the Ben Thanh Market for last-minute souvenir shopping — practice bargaining for lacquerware, silk, coffee, and handicrafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km from HCMC, ~150,000 VND entry + transport) — the extraordinary underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong fighters during the war. Book a shared tour from District 1 (~200,000–300,000 VND including transport). Return to HCMC by late afternoon. Pack your bags and enjoy a final stroll through District 1.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in District 1 with views of the HCMC skyline — try Cuc Gach Quan (traditional Vietnamese home-cooking in a heritage villa) or a rooftop spot on Bui Vien. Raise a glass of Saigon Beer to an incredible 10-day journey through Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Cambodian-style pork noodle soup) at a local HCMC breakfast spot — a southern Vietnamese staple (~40,000–60,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Banh Mi from a Saigon street cart, or a quick Com Tam lunch near Ben Thanh Market (~40,000–70,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cuc Gach Quan (10 Dang Tat Street, Tan Dinh) — Vietnamese home-style cooking in a beautiful heritage setting (~200,000–350,000 VND per person, book in advance) or a budget-friendly final feast on Bui Vien Street.

day_by_day.notes: If departing from Tan Son Nhat Airport, allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. The airport is approximately 30–45 minutes from District 1 by Grab (~80,000–120,000 VND). Pick up Vietnamese drip coffee (Ca Phe) and Pho spice packets as gifts — widely available at Ben Thanh Market. This concludes your 10-day Vietnam adventure spanning Hanoi, Ha Long Bay, Hue, Hoi An, and Ho Chi Minh City.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.date: Day 1 – April 15, 2027 (Arrival Day)
day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in the Old Quarter (approx. 45 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the narrow, atmospheric lanes of the Old Quarter – explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the iconic Hoan Kiem Lake promenade just minutes from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk around Hoan Kiem Lake and visit the illuminated Ngoc Son Temple on Jade Island. Ease into Hanoi's vibrant street-food scene with a guided premium street food tasting tour departing from the hotel – sample bun cha, banh mi, and fresh spring rolls at curated local stalls.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack at hotel upon check-in or grab pho bo (beef pho) at the renowned Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street, a short walk from the hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca Thang Long – a historic Old Quarter institution famous for its signature cha ca (turmeric-marinated fish with dill), paired with local Hanoi Bia Hoi craft beer or Vietnamese wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. April in Hanoi is warm and occasionally humid (~28°C); light breathable clothing recommended. Keep first evening relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.date: Day 2 – April 16, 2027 (Hanoi Deep Dive)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning tai chi session beside Hoan Kiem Lake (locals gather from 06:00 – a free, authentic cultural experience). Follow with a premium guided cyclo tour through the 36 ancient guild streets of the Old Quarter, learning the history of each trade street. Visit the ornate Bach Ma Temple – Hanoi's oldest temple, hidden within the Old Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first university, founded in 1070. Explore the five courtyards, turtle stele pavilions, and serene gardens. Afterward, visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology for a world-class deep dive into the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam with English-speaking expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (premium reserved front-row seats). Post-show, explore the vibrant Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri–Sun) for handicrafts and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Cafe Giang – birthplace of Hanoi's famous egg coffee (ca phe trung), a must-try cultural institution
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Dac Kim on Hang Manh Street – an Old Quarter legend for grilled pork vermicelli, made famous internationally
meals.dinner: Fine dining at La Badiane – a French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant set in a beautiful colonial villa, offering a premium tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Water Puppet Theatre tickets and La Badiane in advance. Temple of Literature closes on Mondays. The Museum of Ethnology is a 15-min taxi ride from the Old Quarter.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Culture & Ho Chi Minh Quarter)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (open mornings only, typically 07:30–10:30; closed Mon & Fri). Explore the Presidential Palace grounds, Ho Chi Minh's iconic stilt house on the lake, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Dress modestly and arrive early to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the French Quarter – stroll past the grand Opera House (Hanoi Opera House), the colonial-era Post Office, and St. Joseph's Cathedral. Browse premium silk and lacquerware boutiques on Hang Gai Street. Visit the Hoa Lo Prison Museum ('Hanoi Hilton') for a sobering and important historical perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop bar of the Sofitel Legend Metropole or Summit Lounge at the Pan Pacific Hanoi with panoramic city views. Explore the sophisticated Bar Betta or Polite Pub in the Old Quarter for craft cocktails infused with Vietnamese botanicals.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi at Banh Mi 25 on Hang Ca Street – consistently rated among Hanoi's best; pair with Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at KOTO (Know One Teach One) – a social enterprise restaurant near the Temple of Literature serving refined Vietnamese cuisine while training disadvantaged youth
meals.dinner: Dinner at Maison Vie – a premium Vietnamese restaurant in the French Quarter offering modern interpretations of Vietnamese classics in an elegant colonial setting

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed Monday and Friday and during national holidays. Photography is restricted inside the mausoleum. Smart casual dress required for evening venues.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – April 18, 2027 (Hanoi to Ha Long Bay – Luxury Cruise Embarkation)
day_by_day.morning: Hotel checkout and private luxury transfer to Ha Long Bay cruise port (approx. 3.5 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Red River Delta countryside. Arrive at the harbor and board your premium overnight cruise (recommended: Indochine Premium, Paradise Elegance, or Orchid Classic – 5-star junk boats with private balcony cabins).
day_by_day.afternoon: Set sail into the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Ha Long Bay. Afternoon kayaking or bamboo boat excursion through hidden limestone caves and secret lagoons (Luon Cave, Dark and Bright Cave). Swim in the emerald waters of a secluded cove.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset on the sundeck with complimentary cocktails and canapés as the bay turns golden. Squid fishing experience off the stern of the boat under the stars. Onboard cooking demonstration featuring fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese and Western breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch aboard the cruise – fresh seafood set menu including steamed clams, grilled squid, and spring rolls as the boat departs the harbor
meals.dinner: Premium 5-course candlelit dinner on the cruise deck featuring whole steamed sea bass, lobster, and local specialties with Vietnamese wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Pack an overnight bag for the cruise; leave larger luggage at the hotel (most boutique hotels offer luggage storage). Bring seasickness medication if prone. April weather is generally pleasant in Ha Long Bay – warm with low winds.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19, 2027 (Ha Long Bay – Return to Hanoi, Fly to Hoi An)
day_by_day.morning: Early sunrise yoga on the sundeck. Morning excursion to a floating fishing village (Cua Van or Vung Vieng) by kayak or rowboat to meet local fishermen. Return to the boat for a premium brunch as the cruise heads back to port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at the harbor (~12:00). Private transfer back to Hanoi (3.5 hours). Head directly to Noi Bai Airport for an afternoon domestic flight to Da Nang (multiple carriers: Vietnam Airlines, Bamboo Airways – approx. 1 hr 15 min flight). Private transfer from Da Nang Airport to Hoi An Ancient Town (approx. 30 min).
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury boutique hotel in Hoi An (recommended: Anantara Hoi An Resort, La Siesta Premium, or The Nam Hai). Evening leisure stroll through the illuminated Hoi An Ancient Town – a UNESCO World Heritage Site glowing with hundreds of silk lanterns.

meals.breakfast: Included brunch aboard the Ha Long Bay cruise
meals.lunch: Light meal at the harbor or airport lounge before flight
meals.dinner: First dinner in Hoi An at The Cargo Club – a beloved riverside restaurant offering panoramic views of the Thu Bon River with an exceptional Vietnamese and Western fusion menu; try the white rose dumplings and cao lau

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flight Hanoi–Da Nang in advance. Confirm Ha Long cruise checkout time to plan flight timing carefully. Hoi An Ancient Town is car-free – explore on foot or by bicycle.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – April 20, 2027 (Hoi An – Ancient Town & Craft Villages)
day_by_day.morning: Private guided walking tour of Hoi An Ancient Town – visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Cau Nhat Ban), the Phung Hung Ancient House, the Fujian Chinese Assembly Hall, and the Tan Ky Merchant House. Learn about the town's history as a 16th-century Southeast Asian trading port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Bicycle excursion to the surrounding craft villages: Thanh Ha Pottery Village (watch artisans shape clay by hand) and Van Phuc Silk Village (see traditional loom weaving). Optional: premium tailoring consultation at one of Hoi An's world-renowned custom tailors (Yaly Couture or A Dong Silk) – order a bespoke ao dai or suit.
day_by_day.evening: Join a premium Hoi An lantern-making workshop and release your handmade lantern on the Thu Bon River during the monthly Full Moon Lantern Festival (check date) or as a standalone experience. Explore the vibrant night market on An Hoi Island.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street – Anthony Bourdain's favorite banh mi spot, an absolute Hoi An institution
meals.lunch: Cao lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at Ba Buoi on Phan Chu Trinh – only authentic when made with water from the ancient Cham wells
meals.dinner: Dinner at Morning Glory Restaurant by chef Trinh Diem Vy – the gold standard of Hoi An dining, serving refined Central Vietnamese cuisine in a beautifully restored ancient house

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An Ancient Town entrance tickets are required (approx. VND 120,000). The tailoring consultation should happen today for a 2-day turnaround pickup. Bicycle rentals are widely available near most hotels.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 – April 21, 2027 (Hoi An – Cooking Class, Beach & My Son Sanctuary)
day_by_day.morning: Premium Vietnamese cooking class at the Red Bridge Cooking School or Morning Glory Cooking School – begin with a guided market tour at Hoi An Central Market to select fresh ingredients, then learn to prepare 4–5 signature Central Vietnamese dishes including white rose dumplings, banh xeo (sizzling crepes), and fresh spring rolls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day excursion to My Son Sanctuary – a UNESCO World Heritage Site of ancient Cham Hindu temple ruins set dramatically in a jungle valley (approx. 40 min from Hoi An). Private guide provides historical context of the Champa Kingdom. Return to Hoi An for a late afternoon at An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach – pristine and less crowded than Da Nang.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar. Return to Hoi An for a relaxed evening. Optional: premium spa treatment at the hotel or at Palmarosa Spa (award-winning, set in a colonial villa).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch prepared and enjoyed during the cooking class – a feast of your own creation
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango Rooms – a vibrant, creative Vietnamese-fusion restaurant on the riverside run by a Vietnamese-American chef; known for innovative cocktails and bold flavors

day_by_day.notes: My Son Sanctuary is best visited in the morning to avoid afternoon heat; adjust schedule if preferred. Bring insect repellent and sun protection for My Son. Collect tailored clothing order if placed on Day 6.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22, 2027 (Hoi An to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Hoi An. Last stroll through the Ancient Town, pick up premium lacquerware, silk, or handcrafted souvenirs. Hotel checkout and private transfer to Da Nang Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fly Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) – approx. 1 hour 20 min. Private luxury transfer to hotel in District 1 (recommended: Park Hyatt Saigon, The Reverie Saigon, or Capella Hanoi equivalent in HCMC). Check in and freshen up. Afternoon exploration of the French Colonial Quarter – visit Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon, the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel), and the Reunification Palace.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at Chill Sky Bar (Level 26, AB Tower) or EON Heli Bar (Bitexco Financial Tower) for spectacular panoramic views of the glittering HCMC skyline at dusk. Explore the electric energy of Bui Vien Walking Street for a taste of Saigon's legendary nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Hoi An
meals.lunch: Banh mi or com tam (broken rice) at a local eatery near Da Nang Airport or airport lounge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Noir – Dining in the Dark, a unique Saigon dining experience where you eat in complete darkness served by visually impaired staff; the multi-course Vietnamese menu is exceptional and the experience unforgettable

day_by_day.notes: Book Noir restaurant well in advance – it fills up quickly. The Reunification Palace closes at 16:00; time arrival accordingly. HCMC traffic can be heavy – allow extra transfer time.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 – April 23, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City – History, Culture & Street Food)
day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the War Remnants Museum – one of the most powerful and important museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War with striking photography and artifacts. Follow with a visit to the Ben Thanh Market for a sensory immersion into local commerce and street food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium half-day excursion to the Cu Chi Tunnels (approx. 1.5 hours from HCMC) – explore the extraordinary 250km underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong fighters. Opt for the less-touristy Ben Duoc section for a more authentic experience with private guide. Return to HCMC for a late afternoon visit to the Jade Emperor Pagoda – a stunning Taoist temple filled with intricate carvings and incense smoke.
day_by_day.evening: Premium Saigon street food tour by motorbike (private, 2-person xe om) – a thrilling way to navigate the city's back alleys and discover hidden local eateries serving banh xeo, hu tieu, and che desserts. End the evening with cocktails at The Long Bar at Park Hyatt or Whisky & Cream for a sophisticated nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pho at Pho Le on Nguyen Trai Street – a legendary HCMC pho institution open since the 1970s
meals.lunch: Com tam Thuan Kieu – premium broken rice with grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, and steamed egg at a beloved local institution near Ben Thanh
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Anan Saigon by Chef Peter Cuong Franklin – a Michelin-recognized restaurant reinterpreting Vietnamese street food through a premium lens; the pho foie gras and banh mi wagyu are legendary

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum can be emotionally intense; allow time to process. Cu Chi Tunnels are claustrophobic – skip the tunnel crawl if needed. Book Anan Saigon well in advance.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 – April 24, 2027 (Final Day – Mekong Delta Excursion & Departure)
day_by_day.morning: Early premium day trip to the Mekong Delta (My Tho or Ben Tre province, approx. 1.5 hours from HCMC). Private boat excursion through narrow waterways and mangrove channels. Visit a coconut candy workshop, a honey bee farm, and a floating market. Enjoy a traditional Mekong lunch with fresh river fish cooked in a clay pot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ho Chi Minh City by early afternoon. Final shopping for premium Vietnamese goods – visit Dong Khoi Street for high-end lacquerware, silk, and coffee (Trung Nguyen or Highlands Coffee flagship stores). Visit a premium Vietnamese coffee shop for a final ca phe sua da (Vietnamese iced milk coffee) – a perfect farewell ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a restaurant of choice based on personal highlights of the trip. Private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat Airport for departure. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days across Vietnam's most iconic destinations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure for Mekong Delta
meals.lunch: Traditional Mekong Delta lunch in Ben Tre – elephant ear fish (ca tai tuong) wrapped in rice paper with fresh herbs, served riverside
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Xu Restaurant Lounge – a sophisticated HCMC institution serving modern Vietnamese cuisine with an outstanding cocktail program and elegant colonial-chic ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer accordingly – allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Mekong Delta return timing should be planned around flight schedule. Consider purchasing premium Vietnamese coffee, silk, and lacquerware as final souvenirs. Ensure all tailored items from Hoi An are packed.
